title: Obesity
summary: Obesity is a disease, not a character flaw. Your gut bacteria help decide how much fat your body stores.
intro: Obesity is a chronic disease shaped by genes, hormones, environment and the trillions of bacteria in your gut. It isn't a failure of willpower. This six-part series walks through the evidence and what you can do about it.

title: Rheumatoid Arthritis
summary: Gut and mouth bacteria differ in rheumatoid arthritis; fiber and diet show modest, early benefits.
intro: Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease of the joints, but research suggests it may begin at the body's mucosal surfaces, including the gut and gums. Human studies show the microbiome looks different in RA, and mouse studies show certain gut bacteria can drive arthritis. Diet and fiber show modest early benefits as additions to medical treatment, not replacements for it.

title: Type 2 Diabetes
summary: How gut bacteria influence blood sugar, metformin and insulin sensitivity, and how diet can help.
intro: People with type 2 diabetes tend to carry fewer fiber-fermenting, butyrate-producing gut bacteria, and the most common diabetes drug, metformin, appears to work partly through the gut. Human trials show that diet changes the gut in ways that can help blood sugar, but the gut is one lever among several and supports medical care rather than replacing it.

articles.title: How gut bacteria shape blood sugar and type 2 diabetes
articles.blurb: What human studies show about gut bacteria, metformin, personal blood sugar responses to food and lean-donor stool transplants.

title: IBS & Digestion
summary: How gut bacteria relate to IBS and bloating, and what probiotics, low-FODMAP and fermented foods really do.
intro: Irritable bowel syndrome is now understood as a disorder of gut-brain interaction, and gut bacteria are part of that picture: IBS can start after a stomach infection, and the gut community often looks different. But microbes are one piece of a larger system, and no diet or supplement cures IBS. These articles cover what the research shows and which approaches have real evidence behind them.

title: Crohn's & Colitis
summary: How gut bacteria shape Crohn's and ulcerative colitis, and which microbiome treatments have real trial evidence.
intro: Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis are lifelong inflammatory conditions in which the immune system attacks the gut. Genes, environment and gut bacteria all play a part, and the microbiome is one of the most studied pieces. These articles cover what the research shows and which bacteria-focused treatments have been tested in trials.

title: Fatty Liver Disease
summary: How gut bacteria and a leaky gut feed liver fat, and what helps protect the liver.
intro: Fatty liver disease, now called MASLD, affects roughly 3 in 10 adults worldwide, and most don't know they have it. Because blood from the gut flows straight to the liver, gut bacteria and a leaky gut lining can push the liver toward storing fat. Mouse studies show that bacteria can cause fatty liver. Human studies show strong links but less proof of cause.

title: Heart Health
summary: How gut bacteria shape heart risk through TMAO, inflammation, blood pressure and cholesterol.
intro: Gut bacteria turn some foods into compounds that can either raise or lower heart risk. Large human studies link the gut-made compound TMAO to heart attacks and strokes, though whether it actually causes them is still debated. Fiber and fermented foods have modest, real effects on blood pressure, cholesterol and inflammation that can add to good medical care.

title: Mood & Gut-Brain
summary: How gut bacteria and the brain communicate, and what diet and probiotics can realistically do for mood.
intro: Your gut and brain talk all the time through nerves, hormones, the immune system and chemicals made by gut bacteria. Animal studies show gut microbes can change behavior. In people, the evidence is mostly links plus a few small trials. Food appears to support mood, but it adds to proper treatment and doesn't replace it.
